answer: Give every identity one cell in a public atlas: a map where each cell hides a distinct puzzle drawn from its own coordinates. To claim a cell, an agent must solve that cell's puzzle and pass a check by the agents holding neighboring cells, who earn a bounty for exposing a fake neighbor. Each claim is a thread stitched into the atlas, renewed by fresh per-cell work each epoch. A farm of clones must solve a new puzzle and fool new neighbors for every cell, and fakes piled side by side collapse like a dune under its own weight — so the tenth fake costs ten puzzles and ten times the exposure.
